Listen to this article Share As consumer expectations shift toward larger television screens, brighter displays, and more versatile home entertainment experiences, global electronics manufacturer TCL is positioning its SQD-Mini LED technology as a major step forward in premium television performance, combining quantum-dot innovation, precision backlighting, and large-screen manufacturing capabilities. Advertisement Advertisement The development reflects an evolving global display industry in which manufacturers are increasingly challenged to deliver superior brightness, colour accuracy, contrast and durability without compromising the affordability of large-format televisions. For much of the past decade, OLED technology has occupied a prominent position in the premium television segment, largely because of its ability to switch off individual pixels to produce absolute blacks and an essentially infinite contrast ratio. However, TCL maintains that the industry’s next phase of innovation must also address the performance and manufacturing limitations associated with organic display materials.OLED’s organic light-emitting components are susceptible to gradual degradation, potentially affecting brightness and colour performance over time. Prolonged exposure to static images, including gaming interfaces, news tickers and streaming menus, can also create a risk of permanent image retention, commonly described as burn-in.Industry comparisons cited in the product narrative place OLED lifespan at approximately 30,000 hours and peak brightness at around 2,000 nits, although actual performance varies considerably by model, usage and operating conditions. Manufacturing costs can also increase significantly at larger screen sizes, particularly in the 85-inch and 98-inch categories, where organic material deposition presents additional production challenges. Advertisement According to TCL, these considerations have strengthened the case for advanced Mini LED technologies capable of delivering high brightness, precise lighting control and greater manufacturing efficiency across increasingly popular large-screen formats. TCL’s response has been the progressive development of its C7 television series, supported by the company’s vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities and sustained investment in quantum dot research, backlight engineering and display optimisation. Advertisement The evolution began with the C725 in 2021, which introduced quantum dot colour technology to the mid-range segment. In 2022, the C735 expanded the series’ performance capabilities with a 144Hz refresh rate, while the C745 followed in 2023 with full-array local dimming and HDR peak brightness of up to 1,000 nits. Further advances came in 2024 with the C755 and its C805 variant, which introduced QD-Mini LED technology to the series, offering up to 1,344 local dimming zones and peak brightness of 1,600 nits. Advertisement Advertisement The C7K followed in 2025 with a claimed peak brightness of up to 3,000 nits, reflecting continued improvements in backlight precision, dimming control and high-dynamic-range performance.Building on these developments, TCL’s C7L introduces SQD-Mini LED technology to the C7 family, combining up to 3,000 nits peak brightness, up to 2,176 precise dimming zones on the 98-inch model and a 5-nanometre Ultra Colour Filter designed to improve colour purity and display performance. The company attributes the commercial viability of these technologies partly to TCL CSOT, its panel-manufacturing division, whose industrial scale supports the integration of advanced display components into television products intended for wider consumer markets. TCL says the development of SQD-Mini LED represents more than an incremental product upgrade, bringing together panel manufacturing, quantum dot research and sophisticated backlight engineering within a unified display system. The technology also arrives at a time when television usage patterns are changing across Nigeria and the wider Middle East and Africa region. Consumers are increasingly seeking larger screens that can accommodate multiple entertainment activities, including movie streaming, live sports, console gaming and smart home connectivity. TCL identifies televisions measuring 75 inches and above as a particularly important growth segment, although the pace of growth varies across individual markets. These changing preferences are placing greater emphasis on display brightness, motion performance, colour reproduction and the ability to maintain picture quality under different lighting conditions. For Nigerian households, where televisions are frequently used in brightly lit living spaces, TCL believes SQD-Mini LED offers a compelling combination of high peak brightness and precise backlight management. Unlike OLED displays, which rely on self-emissive organic pixels, SQD-Mini LED televisions use inorganic LED backlighting alongside quantum dot colour technology. This architecture avoids the organic-pixel burn-in mechanism associated with OLED and supports high-brightness performance, although overall product longevity remains dependent on component quality, operating conditions and usage. TCL further maintains that the manufacturing efficiency of Mini LED technology makes it particularly suitable for larger screen sizes, helping manufacturers deliver premium viewing experiences without the same production constraints associated with very large OLED panels. With the C7L, the company is seeking to strengthen its position in the premium television market by offering a display platform designed for the demands of modern home entertainment, from cinematic content and live sporting events to fast-paced gaming and everyday streaming. The TCL SQD-Mini LED television range is available through SIMS Digital Centres nationwide and online via SIMS TCL Store.
